learnings: Short-term (5-day holds), best in both 2020-23 and 2024-25: Uptrend + close back above 9-day MA after a dip / mirror (long, 5d) median Sharpe 0.24 then 0.24, win 53% in 2024-25; 20-day EMA crosses 50-day EMA (short, 5d) median Sharpe 0.12 then 0.39, win 50% in 2024-25; RSI(2) < 10 above 200-day / > 90 below (Connors) (short, 5d) median Sharpe 0.10 then 0.11, win 56% in 2024-25; 20-day EMA crosses 50-day EMA (long, 5d) median Sharpe 0.10 then 0.38, win 53% in 2024-25.

Short-term (5-day holds) that worked over 2007-2026 but failed in 2024-25: 20-day closing breakout (high / low) (long, 5d) full 0.11 vs 2024-25 -0.18; 55-day closing breakout (high / low) (long, 5d) full 0.22 vs 2024-25 -0.08.

Long-term (10-40 day holds), best in both 2020-23 and 2024-25: Bullish / bearish RSI divergence (long, 10d) median Sharpe 0.30 then 0.39, win 54% in 2024-25; Uptrend + close back above 9-day MA after a dip / mirror (long, 20d) median Sharpe 0.34 then 0.20, win 50% in 2024-25; MACD cross with the 200-day trend (long, 10d) median Sharpe 0.36 then 0.18, win 48% in 2024-25; MACD cross with the 200-day trend (long, 20d) median Sharpe 0.26 then 0.18, win 45% in 2024-25.

Long-term (10-40 day holds) that worked over 2007-2026 but failed in 2024-25: 55-day closing breakout (high / low) (long, 40d) full 0.16 vs 2024-25 -0.80; 20-day closing breakout (high / low) (long, 40d) full 0.17 vs 2024-25 -0.36; 55-day closing breakout (high / low) (long, 10d) full 0.27 vs 2024-25 -0.26.

By family, median Sharpe 2007-18 → 2020-23 → 2024-25: Mean reversion long-term -0.14 → -0.20 → +0.08; Crossover long-term -0.03 → +0.01 → +0.05; Mean reversion + trend long-term -0.01 → +0.07 → +0.04; Mean reversion + trend short-term -0.02 → -0.09 → +0.03; Mean reversion short-term -0.18 → -0.20 → +0.03; Divergence long-term -0.22 → -0.27 → -0.01; Pullback in trend short-term -0.10 → -0.01 → -0.12; Breakout short-term +0.15 → +0.06 → -0.14; Divergence short-term -0.24 → -0.12 → -0.17; Pullback in trend long-term +0.03 → +0.02 → -0.18; Crossover + trend long-term +0.09 → +0.25 → -0.20; Crossover short-term -0.09 → -0.09 → -0.21; Breakout long-term +0.12 → +0.12 → -0.23; Crossover + trend short-term +0.06 → -0.06 → -0.39.

After a close 3% below the 9-day MA (3175 cases): touches the (falling) 9-day MA within 20 days in 96% of cases (median 6 days) but gets back to the 9-day MA level of the signal day only 50% of the time; average drawdown before that -4.0% (worst -31%), return after 10 days -0.08% (up 49% of the time).

After a close 5% below the 9-day MA (1186 cases): touches the (falling) 9-day MA within 20 days in 96% of cases (median 7 days) but gets back to the 9-day MA level of the signal day only 43% of the time; average drawdown before that -5.2% (worst -33%), return after 10 days -0.36% (up 48% of the time).

After a close 7% below the 9-day MA (474 cases): touches the (falling) 9-day MA within 20 days in 97% of cases (median 7 days) but gets back to the 9-day MA level of the signal day only 40% of the time; average drawdown before that -6.5% (worst -34%), return after 10 days -0.23% (up 48% of the time).

After a close 10% below the 9-day MA (95 cases): touches the (falling) 9-day MA within 20 days in 96% of cases (median 6 days) but gets back to the 9-day MA level of the signal day only 40% of the time; average drawdown before that -8.6% (worst -36%), return after 10 days +2.37% (up 61% of the time).
First dip to the 9-day MA in an uptrend (2504 cases): new 20-day high within 20 days 51%, closed below the 50-day 68%, average dip -4.4%, return after 20 days +0.28% (up 51%).
First dip to the 20-day MA in an uptrend (1657 cases): new 20-day high within 20 days 44%, closed below the 50-day 75%, average dip -4.5%, return after 20 days +0.08% (up 49%).
First dip to the 50-day MA in an uptrend (1052 cases): new 20-day high within 20 days 31%, closed below the 50-day 96%, average dip -4.8%, return after 20 days -0.52% (up 45%).
4492 rule x market x holding-period tests: a t-stat around 4.1 is what the luckiest test would show by chance, so prefer rules that work across many markets and in both 2007-18 and 2019+.
